question: How much did Hadrian raise in its latest funding round?

hits.title: Hadrian hits $8 billion as defense tech spending craze endures
hits.snippet: - Hadrian raised nearly $1.4 billion in new funding at a $7.9 billion valuation. - Defense tech startups are benefiting from President Donald Trump's plan to upgrade the U.S. military. - Hadrian CEO Chris Power said the fresh funds will allow it to invest in its workforce and its Opus software platform. ... Riding a wave of enthusiasm for defense tech, manufacturing startup Hadrian said on Thursday that it has closed its latest round of funding at a $7.9 billion valuation, more than quadruple where investors valued the company in January. ... Hadrian, which builds advanced factories for defense and aerospace companies and agencies, raised nearly $1.4 billion in a round led by Baillie Gifford, J.P. Morgan Strategic Investment Group, and a number of others, including Washington Harbour Partners. ... Last year, Hadrian raised $260 million, with funding ... , to build a new ... defense capabilities.

hits.snippet: Defense tech Hadrian announced on Thursday that it had raised a fresh $1.37 billion round at a valuation of $7.87 billion from a mile-long list of well-known investors. ... hits.snippet: Investors are continuing to rally behind the call to reindustrialize American industry, this time by building out a $260 million war chest for automated manufacturing startup Hadrian to scale its factory footprint and make even more machine parts. ... Hadrian is announcing a $260m Series C lead by@foundersfund+@Lux_Capital+@MorganStanley for (Factory Expansion financing). hits.snippet: San Francisco – January 9, 2026 – Cooley advised Hadrian, a company building the next generation of American factories to support national reindustrialization, on its expanded capital led by accounts advised by T. hits.title: Hadrian Raises $260M to Build AI-Powered Factories for America, Adds Full Product Manufacturing, Opens Arizona Site: New capital and factory expansions accelerate the company’s mission to reindustrialize America | Hadrian
hits.snippet: TORRANCE, CA – July 17, 2025 – Hadrian, the advanced manufacturing company building AI-powered factories for America, today announced $260 million in new capital and major expansions of its footprint in California and Arizona. The investment supports nearly five football fields’ worth of new manufacturing space, expanded R&D capacity, and dedicated teams focused on shipbuilding and naval defense production. ... The raise includes $260 million in Series C financing led by existing investors Founders Fund and Lux Capital, and a factory expansion loan facility arranged by Morgan Stanley. This capital will accelerate Hadrian’s ability to deliver not just precision parts but full mission-critical systems. The company now covers the entire advanced manufacturing stack, from raw material to finished products, and supports everything from components to assemblies to complete platforms. With its “Factories-as-a-Service” model, Hadrian can rapidly scale production across key Department of Defense (DOD) areas such as munitions, shipbuilding, and other high-priority programs.
